item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
This chart shows temperature readings made at different times on four days.

| TEMPERATURES | | | | | |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| | 6 a.m. | 9 a.m. | Noon | 3 p.m. | 8 p.m. |
| Monday | 15° | 17° | 20° | 21° | 19° |
| Tuesday | 15° | 15° | 15° | 10° | 9° |
| Wednesday | 8° | 10° | 14° | 13° | 15° |
| Thursday | 8° | 11° | 14° | 17° | 20° |

When was the highest temperature recorded?

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Temperature for Week graph]

The graph above shows the daily high and low temperatures for a week.

On which day is the difference between the high and low temperatures the greatest?
reference_items.figure_description:
A plot titled "Temperature for Week". The vertical axis is labeled "Temperature" with grid lines marked at 20°, 25°, 30°, 35°, 40°, and 45°. The horizontal axis is labeled "Day" with vertical grid lines marked at Sun., Mon., Tues., Wed., Thu., Fri., and Sat.
A legend on the right shows a filled black circle labeled "High Temp." and an open circle labeled "Low Temp."
The points plotted for each day are:
- Sun.: High Temp. at 39°, Low Temp. at 25°
- Mon.: High Temp. at 42°, Low Temp. at 24°
- Tues.: High Temp. at ~34°, Low Temp. at ~28°
- Wed.: High Temp. at 30°, Low Temp. at 20°
- Thu.: High Temp. at 26°, Low Temp. at ~23°
- Fri.: High Temp. at ~36°, Low Temp. at 25°
- Sat.: High Temp. at 45°, Low Temp. at 30°
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
When Tracy left for school, the temperature was minus 3 degrees.

[Image: Thermometer showing minus 3 degrees]

At recess, the temperature was 5 degrees.

[Image: Thermometer showing 5 degrees]

How many degrees did the temperature rise?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two identical vertical thermometers are shown, one below the other:
1. The top thermometer has a scale marked with tick marks at intervals of 1 unit. Major tick marks are labeled on both sides at 10, 0, and -10. Intermediate longer tick marks appear at 5 and -5. The black liquid column rises from the bulb at the bottom to 3 units below 0 (-3 degrees).
2. The bottom thermometer has the same scale and markings (labeled at 10, 0, and -10). The black liquid column rises from the bulb to 5 units above 0 (5 degrees).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the number of cartons of milk sold each day of a week at a school.

[Image: Bar graph]

How many cartons of milk did the school sell on Monday?

Answer: ____
reference_items.figure_description:
A vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled "Number Sold" with major grid lines and labels at 10, 20, 30, and 40. The horizontal axis is labeled "Day" with five days labeled: "Mon.", "Tues.", "Wed.", "Thurs.", "Fri.". All bars are shaded grey. The bar heights are:
- Mon.: halfway between 20 and 30 (height 25)
- Tues.: level with 20
- Wed.: level with 30
- Thurs.: halfway between 10 and 20 (height 15)
- Fri.: halfway between 30 and 40 (height 35)

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The figure shows how Mary spent her time one day.

[Image: Pie chart showing how Mary spent her time]

What percent of time altogether did she spend playing and doing homework?
reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart showing how Mary spent her time one day, divided into five labeled sectors:
- "Homework 10%": from the 12 o'clock vertical radius clockwise to roughly 1 o'clock.
- "Sleeping & Resting 40%": from roughly 1 o'clock clockwise to the 6 o'clock vertical radius.
- "Going to School 25%": from the 6 o'clock vertical radius clockwise to the 9 o'clock horizontal radius.
- "Eating 10%": from the 9 o'clock horizontal radius clockwise to roughly 10 o'clock.
- "Playing 15%": from roughly 10 o'clock clockwise to the 12 o'clock vertical radius.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
